title: Short Stuff: Korean Fan Death
summary: Short Stuff episode on "fan death," the Korean superstition that sleeping in a room with an electric fan running can kill you. The hosts cover how widespread the belief is in Korea (fan warnings, timers, cracked windows), the 2005 Korean Consumer Protection Board summer hazards warning, and the claim of twenty deaths between 2003 and 2005. They note the belief appears to date from the early 1970s despite fans existing since 1900, and speculate it may have been promoted during an energy-conservation campaign after the oil embargo. They then go through proposed explanations: dehydration from sweating, oxygen being chopped up or mutilated, suffocation from recirculated carbon dioxide, hypothermia, and low air pressure near the face (Samsung Medical Center claim), which they judge unconvincing. They also note the US EPA warning against aiming fans at people in temperatures above 90 degrees Fahrenheit, and that fan death is not reported elsewhere in the world.
topics: Consumer Protection Board summer hazards warning

segments.title: Introduction to fan death
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the Korean superstition that sleeping with a fan on can kill you, and note how seriously Koreans take it.

segments.title: Belief in Korea and official warnings
segments.summary: The hosts describe how widely the belief is held in Korea, including fan timers, manufacturer warnings, and people sleeping with windows open. They cite the 2005 Consumer Protection Board warning and a claim of twenty deaths between 2003 and 2005.
topics: Consumer Protection Board summer hazards warning

segments.title: Origins of the belief
segments.summary: The belief appears to date from the early 1970s even though fans existed in Korea since 1900. The hosts speculate it may have been promoted during an energy-conservation campaign after the oil embargo, while noting this is unverified. They suggest a likely origin: someone finding a dead person in a room with a fan running.

segments.title: EPA heat warning
segments.summary: The hosts mention the US EPA advice not to aim a fan at yourself when temperatures exceed 90 degrees Fahrenheit, and note this lends some credence to one fan death theory.

segments.title: Proposed explanations: dehydration and oxygen
segments.summary: The hosts review theories that fans cause dehydration through faster sweat evaporation, and that fans chop up or mutilate oxygen molecules, reducing available oxygen.

segments.title: Suffocation, hypothermia, and air pressure theories
segments.summary: The hosts discuss suffocation from recirculated carbon dioxide, which they say is implausible because homes are not airtight, and hypothermia, which experts reject because fans move air without cooling it. They also cover a Samsung Medical Center claim that fans reduce air pressure in front of the face, which Skeptoid's Brian Dunning calculated to be too small an effect.

segments.title: Lack of cases elsewhere and closing
segments.summary: The hosts note fan death is not reported anywhere else in the world, suggesting folklore, while Koreans suggest something unique about Korea. They close the episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wrap up the episode and thank listeners.
